root_cause.text: Integer overflow in `xdr_round_up(token_len)` when `token_len` is large causes the rounded value to wrap to a small value, bypassing the length validation in `rxgk_verify_response()` and allowing out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (token_len > len ||` before the existing `xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len` check, ensuring the unrounded length is also validated. The commit message explicitly states "potential integer overflow due to rounding up token_len before checking it, thereby allowing the length check to be bypassed."

bic_trace_step.reason: In `rxgk_verify_response()`, the check `if (xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len)` uses the result of `xdr_round_up(token_len)` which can overflow if `token_len` is large, causing the comparison to use a wrapped small value and bypass the length validation. The code does not include any overflow mitigation, making it vulnerable to integer overflow and subsequent out-of-bounds access.
